subject: maths
title: Primary 2 Numbers to 1000
seo_title: P2 Numbers to 1000 Worksheets: Free Primary 2 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: Numbers up to 1000: counting in tens/hundreds, place values, reading and writing, comparing and ordering, patterns
meta_desc: Free P2 maths practice on numbers to 1000: place value, numerals and words, comparing, ordering, counting in tens and hundreds. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Write 0 for an empty place: four hundred and seven is 407, not 47.
key_sub: In 345 the digit 4 is in the tens place, so its value is 40.
body_html:
Hundreds, tens and ones

A 3-digit number has three places: hundreds, tens and ones. 10 ones make 1 ten. 10 tens make 1 hundred. 10 hundreds make 1000.

A place value chart shows the digit in each place. The place tells you what the digit is worth.

Reading and writing numbers

Say the hundreds first, then “and”, then the tens and ones. If a place is empty, write 0 there. The 0 keeps the other digits in the right places.

NumeralWords
407four hundred and seven
470four hundred and seventy
515five hundred and fifteen
300three hundred
1000one thousand
Words to numerals

Write four hundred and seven in numerals.

4 hundreds, 0 tens and 7 ones. Write 4, 0, 7.

Answer: 407 (not 47 or 4007)

Comparing and ordering

First count the digits: a 3-digit number is greater than a 2-digit number. If both have 3 digits, compare the hundreds, then the tens, then the ones.

Compare

Which is greater, 407 or 470?

Hundreds: 4 = 4. Tens: 0 tens < 7 tens.

Answer: 470 is greater. 407 < 470

> means “is greater than”. < means “is smaller than”. The open side faces the greater number.

Counting in tens and hundreds

Counting on in tens changes the tens digit: 230, 240, 250. Counting on in hundreds changes the hundreds digit: 145, 245, 345. When there are 10 tens, rename them as 1 hundred: 580, 590, 600.

Patterns and word problems

To find the rule of a pattern, find how much each number goes up or down. In a word problem, draw a bar model to see what to find.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Leaving out the zero (four hundred and seven → 47)Write 0 for the empty tens place: 407
Writing each part you hear (four hundred and seven → 4007)A number in the hundreds has 3 digits: 407
Mixing up 407 and 470407 has 0 tens and 7 ones. 470 has 7 tens and 0 ones
Giving the digit, not its value (the 4 in 345 is 4)The 4 is in the tens place: 40
Comparing the first digits only (99 > 189)Count the digits first: 189 > 99
Not renaming when counting in tens (590, 5100)10 tens make 1 hundred: 590, 600

faq.q: What is taught in P2 numbers to 1000?
faq.a: Primary 2 students count in tens and hundreds, read and write numbers up to 1000 in numerals and in words, find the value of each digit, compare and order numbers, and continue number patterns.

faq.q: How do I explain place value to my child?
faq.a: Use bundles or blocks: 10 ones make a ten and 10 tens make a hundred. Then 346 is 3 hundreds, 4 tens and 6 ones, so the 4 is worth 40.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with numbers to 1000?
faq.a: The most common mistake is leaving out a zero, such as writing four hundred and seven as 47. Children also mix up 407 and 470, or give the digit instead of its value.

faq.q: Is numbers to 1000 in the MOE syllabus?
faq.a: Yes. Numbers up to 1000, including counting in tens and hundreds, place values, reading and writing, comparing and ordering, and patterns, are part of Whole Numbers in the MOE 2021 Primary 2 Mathematics syllabus.

items.e: A flat is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 2 hundreds, 3 tens and 4 ones make 234. Start with the flats: 200. Then the rods: 230. Then the cubes: 234.
A flat is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 1 hundred, 5 tens and 2 ones make 152. Count the flats, then the rods, then the small cubes.
Each rod is 1 ten. There are 5 rods, so there are 5 tens. The number is 352.

items.q: What number do the place value discs show?
items.e: Find the value of each group of discs: 3 discs of 100 = 300, 4 discs of 10 = 40, 2 discs of 1 = 2. Then put them together: 342.
A flat is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 3 hundreds, 0 tens and 6 ones make 306. There are no tens, so write 0 in the tens place.
Each flat is 1 hundred. There are 4 flats, so there are 4 hundreds. The number is 426.

items.q: Which number has 5 hundreds, 3 tens and 8 ones?
items.e: Write the hundreds digit first, then the tens, then the ones: 5, 3, 8. That is 538.
A flat is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 4 hundreds, 2 tens and 0 ones make 420. There are no ones, so write 0 in the ones place.

items.q: Which is the same as 604?
items.e: 604 is 6 hundreds, 0 tens and 4 ones. That is 6 hundreds and 4 ones. (6 hundreds and 4 tens is 640.)

items.q: What number do the place value discs show?
items.e: Find the value of each group of discs: 5 discs of 100 = 500, 8 discs of 1 = 8. Then put them together: 508. There are no 10 discs, so write 0 in the tens place.
A flat is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 2 hundreds, 6 tens and 5 ones make 265. Count the rods in tens: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60.

items.q: Which number has 7 hundreds and 4 ones?
items.e: There are no tens, so write 0 in the tens place: 7, 0, 4. That is 704.

items.q: How many tens are in 709?
items.e: 709 is 7 hundreds, 0 tens and 9 ones. The 0 shows that there are no tens.

items.q: What number do the place value discs show?
items.e: Find the value of each group of discs: 2 discs of 100 = 200, 7 discs of 10 = 70. Then put them together: 270. There are no 1 discs, so write 0 in the ones place.

items.q: Which is the same as 851?
items.e: Read the digits from the left: 8 is in the hundreds place, 5 is in the tens place and 1 is in the ones place. 851 = 8 hundreds, 5 tens and 1 one.
A flat is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 6 hundreds, 1 ten and 3 ones make 613. Count the flats in hundreds: 100, 200 … 600.

items.q: Which number has 2 hundreds and 9 tens?
items.e: 2 hundreds and 9 tens is 200 + 90 = 290. There are no ones, so the ones digit is 0.

items.q: How many hundreds make 1000?
items.e: Count in hundreds: 100, 200, 300 … 1000. That is 10 hundreds. 10 hundreds make 1000.
There are 12 rods. 10 tens make 1 hundred, so 12 tens = 1 hundred and 2 tens. 200 + 120 + 5 = 325.
Each flat is 100. Count in hundreds: 100, 200, 300 … 1000. 10 hundreds make 1000.

sets.title: Read and write numbers in words

items.q: Write four hundred and seven in numerals.
items.e: Four hundred and seven is 4 hundreds, 0 tens and 7 ones: 407. Write 0 for the empty tens place.

items.q: Which is 407 in words?
items.e: 407 is 4 hundreds, 0 tens and 7 ones. Say the hundreds, then the rest: four hundred and seven.

items.q: Write six hundred and thirty in numerals.
items.e: Six hundred and thirty is 6 hundreds, 3 tens and 0 ones: 630. Write 0 for the empty ones place.

items.q: Which is the correct way to write 340 in words?
items.e: 340 is 3 hundreds and 4 tens. 4 tens is forty. Forty has no u: f-o-r-t-y.

items.q: Write this number in words.
items.e: The chart shows 8 hundreds, 0 tens and 6 ones: 806. In words: eight hundred and six.

items.q: Write two hundred and fifteen in numerals.
items.e: Two hundred and fifteen is 2 hundreds, 1 ten and 5 ones: 215.

items.q: Which is 560 in words?
items.e: 560 is 5 hundreds, 6 tens and 0 ones. Say the hundreds, then the rest: five hundred and sixty.

items.q: Write three hundred in numerals.
items.e: Three hundred is 3 hundreds, 0 tens and 0 ones: 300. Write 0 for the empty tens and ones places. Three thousand is 3000.

items.q: Which is 318 in words?
items.e: 318 is 3 hundreds, 1 ten and 8 ones. Say the hundreds, then the rest: three hundred and eighteen. 1 ten and 8 ones is eighteen.

items.q: Write one thousand in numerals.
items.e: One thousand is 10 hundreds: 1000. It has 1 and three zeros.

items.q: Write eight hundred and sixty-four in numerals.
items.e: Eight hundred and sixty-four is 8 hundreds, 6 tens and 4 ones: 864.

items.q: Write this number in words.
items.e: The chart shows 4 hundreds, 7 tens and 0 ones: 470. 7 tens is seventy. In words: four hundred and seventy.

items.q: Which is 740 in words?
items.e: 740 is 7 hundreds, 4 tens and 0 ones. Say the hundreds, then the rest: seven hundred and forty.

items.q: Write seven hundred and fifty in numerals.
items.e: Seven hundred and fifty is 7 hundreds, 5 tens and 0 ones: 750. Write 0 for the empty ones place. Fifty is 5 tens. Fifteen is 15.

items.q: Which is the correct way to write 290 in words?
items.e: 290 is 2 hundreds and 9 tens. 9 tens is ninety. Ninety keeps the e: n-i-n-e-t-y.

items.q: Which is 913 in words?
items.e: 913 is 9 hundreds, 1 ten and 3 ones. Say the hundreds, then the rest: nine hundred and thirteen. 1 ten and 3 ones is thirteen.

items.q: Write five hundred and nineteen in numerals.
items.e: Five hundred and nineteen is 5 hundreds, 1 ten and 9 ones: 519. Nineteen is 19. Ninety is 9 tens.

items.q: Which is 605 in words?
items.e: 605 is 6 hundreds, 0 tens and 5 ones. Say the hundreds, then the rest: six hundred and five.

items.q: Write nine hundred and two in numerals.
items.e: Nine hundred and two is 9 hundreds, 0 tens and 2 ones: 902. Write 0 for the empty tens place.

items.q: Siti writes “three hundred and nine” as 3009. What is the correct numeral?
items.e: Three hundred and nine is 3 hundreds, 0 tens and 9 ones: 309. A number in the hundreds has only 3 digits, so do not write 300 and then 9.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: The hundreds are the same, so compare the tens: 7 tens is more than 4 tens. So 470 is greater than 447. 470 is the greatest.

items.q: Which is correct?
items.e: The hundreds are the same, so compare the tens: 7 tens is more than 0 tens. So 470 is greater than 407. So 407 < 470.

items.q: Which number is the smallest?
items.e: The hundreds are the same, so compare the tens: 9 tens is more than 8 tens. So 298 is greater than 289. 289 is the smallest.

items.q: Use the digits 3, 8 and 5 once each. What is the greatest 3-digit number you can make?
items.e: Put the biggest digit in the hundreds place, then the next biggest: 8, 5, 3. That is 853.

items.q: Which is correct?
items.e: The hundreds are the same, so compare the tens: 5 tens is more than 2 tens. So 352 is greater than 325. So 352 > 325.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: The hundreds are the same, so compare the tens: 3 tens is more than 0 tens. So 530 is greater than 503. 530 is the greatest.

items.q: Arrange the numbers in order, beginning with the smallest: 371, 317, 731
items.e: 731 has 7 hundreds, so it is the greatest. 317 and 371 both have 3 hundreds. Tens: 1 ten < 7 tens, so 317 < 371. Order: 317, 371, 731.

items.q: Which number is the smallest?
items.e: 99 has only 2 digits. The others have 3 digits. So 99 is the smallest, even though 9 is a big digit.

items.q: Which number is between 600 and 650?
items.e: 628 has 6 hundreds and 2 tens, so it is more than 600 and less than 650. 682 and 660 are more than 650. 599 is less than 600.

items.q: Which is correct?
items.e: 189 has 3 digits and 98 has only 2. So 189 is greater. So 98 < 189. Do not look only at the first digit. Count the digits first.

items.q: Arrange the numbers in order, beginning with the smallest: 560, 506, 56
items.e: 56 has only 2 digits, so it is the smallest. 506 and 560 both have 5 hundreds. Tens: 0 tens < 6 tens, so 506 < 560. Order: 56, 506, 560.

items.q: Use the digits 6, 0 and 2 once each. What is the smallest 3-digit number you can make?
items.e: A 3-digit number cannot start with 0. Put the smaller of 2 and 6 first: 2. Then 0, then 6: 206. (026 is just 26, which has only 2 digits.)

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: 1000 has 4 digits. The others have only 3 digits. 1000 is 1 more than 999, so 1000 is the greatest.

items.q: Which is correct?
items.e: The hundreds are the same, so compare the tens: 6 tens is more than 0 tens. So 760 is greater than 706. So 760 > 706.

items.q: Which number is the smallest?
items.e: The hundreds are the same, so compare the tens: 1 ten is more than 0 tens. So 612 is greater than 602. 602 is the smallest.

items.q: Arrange the numbers in order, beginning with the greatest: 849, 894, 489
items.e: 489 has only 4 hundreds, so it is the smallest. 849 and 894 both have 8 hundreds. Tens: 9 tens > 4 tens, so 894 > 849. Order: 894, 849, 489.

items.q: Which number is greater than 509 but smaller than 590?
items.e: 550 is greater than 509 (5 tens > 0 tens) and smaller than 590 (5 tens < 9 tens). 505 is smaller than 509, 595 is greater than 590, and 509 is not greater than itself.

items.q: Use the digits 7, 0 and 4 once each. What is the greatest 3-digit number you can make?
items.e: Biggest digit first: 7. Then 4. The 0 goes last, in the ones place: 740.

items.q: Which is correct?
items.e: 1000 has 4 digits and 999 has only 3. So 1000 is greater. So 999 < 1000.

items.q: Arrange the numbers in order, beginning with the smallest: 625, 652, 256, 265
items.e: 256 and 265 have 2 hundreds, so they come first: 5 tens < 6 tens, so 256 < 265. 625 and 652 have 6 hundreds: 2 tens < 5 tens. Order: 256, 265, 625, 652.

items.q:
What comes next?
230, 240, 250, ☐
items.e: Count on in tens: each number is 10 more. Only the tens digit goes up. 250 + 10 = 260.

items.q:
What comes next?
200, 300, 400, ☐
items.e: Count on in hundreds: each number is 100 more. 400 + 100 = 500.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 0 to 1000 there are 10 equal jumps, so each jump is 100. The arrow is 3 jumps after 500: 600, 700, 800.
The blocks show 245. 1 more ten is 10 more: 245 + 10 = 255. Only the tens digit changes.

items.q:
What comes next?
145, 245, 345, ☐
items.e: Count on in hundreds: only the hundreds digit goes up. 3 hundreds → 4 hundreds: 445.

items.q:
What is the missing number?
610, 620, ☐, 640

What comes next?
480, 470, 460, ☐
items.e: Count back in tens: each number is 10 less. 460 − 10 = 450.

items.q: Add 1 more hundred. What number is it now?
items.e: The blocks show 136. 1 more hundred is 100 more: 136 + 100 = 236. Only the hundreds digit changes.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: Each jump is 10. Count on in tens from 200: 210, 220, 230. (203 counts each jump as 1.)

items.q:
What comes next?
906, 806, 706, ☐
items.e: Count back in hundreds: only the hundreds digit goes down. 706 − 100 = 606.

items.q: How many tens are there in 300?
items.e: 1 hundred is 10 tens. So 3 hundreds are 10 + 10 + 10 = 30 tens.

items.q: What number is 100 more than 856?
items.e: 100 more: the hundreds digit goes up by 1. 8 hundreds → 9 hundreds: 956. (866 is 10 more.)

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 300 to 400 there are 10 equal jumps, so each jump is 10, not 1. The arrow is 2 jumps after 350: 360, 370.

items.q:
What comes next?
570, 580, 590, ☐
items.e: 590 + 10: 9 tens + 1 ten = 10 tens. Rename 10 tens as 1 hundred: 5 hundreds become 6 hundreds. The answer is 600, not 5100.
The blocks show 392. Add 1 rod: now there are 10 rods. Rename 10 tens as 1 hundred. That is 4 hundreds, 0 tens and 2 ones: 402.

items.q: What number is 10 more than 695?
items.e: 695 + 10: 9 tens + 1 ten = 10 tens = 1 hundred. So 6 hundreds become 7 hundreds and the tens digit becomes 0: 705. (795 is 100 more. 696 is 1 more.)

items.q:
What comes next?
720, 710, 700, ☐
items.e: Count back in tens: 700 − 10 = 690. 700 is 70 tens, and 1 ten less is 69 tens = 690.

items.q: 40 tens = ☐. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 10 tens make 1 hundred. 40 tens are 4 groups of 10 tens: 4 hundreds = 400.

items.q: What number is 10 less than 403?
items.e: 403 has 0 tens. Take 1 hundred and rename it as 10 tens: 3 hundreds and 10 tens. Take away 1 ten: 3 hundreds, 9 tens and 3 ones = 393. (303 is 100 less.)

items.q: What number is 100 less than 1000?
items.e: 1000 is 10 hundreds. 1 hundred less is 9 hundreds = 900. (990 is 10 less. 999 is 1 less.)

items.q:
What is the rule for this pattern?
312, 322, 332, 342
items.e: The numbers get bigger. 322 − 312 = 10. The tens digit goes up by 1 each time. The rule is “add 10”.

items.q:
What is the missing number?
455, 465, ☐, 485, 495

Count on in fives. What comes next?
735, 740, 745, ☐
items.e: Each number is 5 more. 745 + 5 = 750. (755 adds 10. 845 adds 100.)

items.q:
What is the rule for this pattern?
865, 765, 665, 565
items.e: The numbers get smaller. 865 − 765 = 100. The hundreds digit goes down by 1 each time. The rule is “subtract 100”.

items.q:
What is the missing number?
980, ☐, 780, 680

What is the 5th number in this pattern?
120, 220, 320, …
items.e: Each number is 100 more. 120 (1st), 220 (2nd), 320 (3rd), 420 (4th), 520 (5th).

items.q:
What comes next?
1000, 900, 800, ☐
items.e: Each number is 100 less. 800 − 100 = 700. (790 is only 10 less. 600 is 200 less. 810 adds 10.)

items.q: Ali has 3 boxes of 100 stickers, 4 packets of 10 stickers and 5 loose stickers. How many stickers does he have?
items.e: 3 boxes of 100 = 300. 4 packets of 10 = 40. 300 + 40 + 5 = 345. (Do not just add 3 + 4 + 5.)

items.q: Mrs Lim buys 6 packs of paper cups for Children’s Day. Each pack has 100 cups. How many cups does she buy?
items.e: Count in hundreds 6 times: 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600. 6 hundreds = 600.

items.q: Mei Ling has 356 stamps. Jun Jie has 100 more stamps than Mei Ling. How many stamps does Jun Jie have?
items.e: Jun Jie’s bar is Mei Ling’s bar and 100 more. 356 + 100 = 456. Only the hundreds digit changes. (366 is 10 more. 256 is 100 fewer.)

items.q: The school library has “seven hundred and eight” story books. Write the number of books in numerals.
items.e: Seven hundred and eight is 7 hundreds, 0 tens and 8 ones: 708. Write 0 for the empty tens place.

items.q: A hawker centre sells 638 plates of chicken rice and 683 bowls of laksa on Saturday. Which does it sell more of?
items.e: Both numbers have 6 hundreds. Compare the tens: 8 tens > 3 tens. So 683 > 638. It sells more laksa.

items.q: Hafiz thinks of a 3-digit number. It has 6 hundreds, 5 ones and no tens. What is his number?
items.e: 6 hundreds, 0 tens and 5 ones: 605. The 0 holds the tens place.

items.q: Raju reads 285 pages. Priya reads 10 fewer pages than Raju. How many pages does Priya read?
items.e: Priya’s bar is 10 shorter than Raju’s. 285 − 10 = 275. (295 is 10 more. 185 is 100 fewer.)

items.q: Ryan has 470 points in a game. He gets 10 points for each star. He gets 3 more stars. How many points does he have now?
items.e: Count on in tens 3 times: 480, 490, 500. (473 adds 3 ones. 770 adds 3 hundreds.)

items.q: For a recycling drive, Class 2A collects 246 cans, Class 2B collects 264 cans and Class 2C collects 226 cans. Which class collects the most cans?
items.e: All three numbers have 2 hundreds. Compare the tens: 6 tens is the most. 264 is the greatest, so Class 2B collects the most.

items.q: Xin Yi’s number is 10 less than 600. What is her number?
items.e: 600 is 60 tens. 1 ten less is 59 tens = 590. (500 is 100 less. 599 is 1 less.)

items.q: Box A has 300 beads. Box B has 200 beads. How many beads are there in all?
items.e: 3 hundreds and 2 hundreds make 5 hundreds. Count on in hundreds from 300: 400, 500. There are 500 beads.

items.q: Mr Tan has 1000 sheets of paper. He gives away 100 sheets. How many sheets does he have left?
items.e: 1000 is 10 hundreds. Take away 1 hundred: 9 hundreds = 900. (990 takes away only 10.)

items.q: Ethan counts on in tens from 340: 350, 360, … He stops at 400. How many numbers does he say after 340?
